approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a score-ranked population of molecular graphs using parents drawn from favored rank ranges. It forms fresh offspring through connected-fragment recombination or ordinary one-, two-, or three-step mutation, rejects invalid identities, duplicates and newly introduced source-relative sulfur patterns, and fits a Gaussian process to count fingerprints and accepted scores from the current session. Correlated posterior samples select each evaluation batch from the fresh pool. After three batches without an incumbent improvement, purchases are restricted to the forty highest predictive means until improvement resumes. Accepted scores update the population and the full training archive.
approach.novelty: Remove the connected-fragment crossover route throughout the session by setting its probability to zero while retaining its branch draw and the inherited ordinary mutation path. This measures whether recombination still contributes under the current stall-conditioned allocator. Same-Parent siblings changed ordinary continuation, residual or mean consumers, or the search controller; they did not isolate this crossover route. Earlier crossover controls used other Parent compositions. The new contrast measures the total presence of the route, including access to its conditional finishing edit, and predicts that removing it changes paid ancestry and reduces useful gain if it remains valuable.

observed_bottleneck: The current stall-masked count-GP Parent n-cf8d309c06de still buys many connected-fragment recombinants, but the conditional value of retaining that route under its current allocator is unmeasured. Its complete Search mean is 0.607030316211131 (population seed deviation 0.030175277546149237); the exact fifteen session logs contain 34,369 requested crossover attempts, 29,808 recombinant pool members and 1,480 recombinant purchases out of 4,350 paid offspring. Full and late incumbent-increment masses are 5.978073077532332 and 1.0224077547621127. Thus productive endpoint progress remains limited despite substantial route exposure; exposure itself does not establish contribution. Exact published summaries reproduce removal deltas -0.04363978685149128 for n-6059424cc614 on the earlier sulfur-gated Parent and -0.054937284705486644 for n-767d2ce08797 on the earlier exchange-free Parent; stall-only removal n-9e5f01d67b9f loses -0.014191741028113602 on the sulfur-gated Parent while its registered stall-escape story fails. These are different host or routing conditions. Catalog qualifications concerning adaptive departure remain, and neither historical losses nor their widths establish the current masked-host contribution. Parent source, all three summary.json/run.log files, all fifteen session logs/trajectories, cited node records and historical source diffs were read and hashed in policy/scratch/r0061-03-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json.
hypothesis: Remove only m-00000000000a on code Parent n-cf8d309c06de: change CONFIG.crossover_probability from 0.45 to exactly 0.0. Every breeding attempt still selects the same first-parent law and consumes the existing single pre-branch Python RNG draw in its original position. The original member_attempts > 40 attenuation still multiplies the active probability by 0.5, leaving it zero. The existing two-parent branch, partner exclusion, connected-fragment constructor and conditional finishing code remain in source but cannot execute. Every attempt therefore enters the existing ordinary route: sample one/two/three mutate calls with probabilities 0.82/0.15/0.03 and stop at the first failed call. Causal path: exposed crossover routing is removed, fresh pool ancestry and purchased identities change, then accepted population and GP training histories change; if the retained route contributes useful discoveries, complete full/late gain and endpoint mean should fall. This is the total adaptive route-removal effect, including absence of conditional finishing access and naturally changed graph RNG consumption. It does not separately identify fragment construction, finishing, RNG or chemistry mediation.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover removal eliminates recombinant purchases and lowers the complete mean by 0.05149
finding_summary.insights: Frequent small improvements did not replace the larger gains supplied by the complete Parent search. The Child produced 305 strict incumbent improvements versus 253, but their mean size fell from 0.023629 to 0.017068; late improvements likewise increased from 76 to 101 while their total gain fell. Stall-restricted batches fell from 88 to 53, so fewer stalls also failed to predict stronger endpoints. Higher parent-beating frequency is not independent support because a single-parent hurdle is easier than the Parent’s better-of-two hurdle. The molecular report narrows the structural explanation: generic scaffold coverage fell from 951 to 878 even though typed scaffold count rose from 1,667 to 1,762. Both size tails disappeared—the Child stayed at 22–47 heavy atoms—but that narrower size range did not preserve endpoint quality. Fragment-excluded similarity changed only from 0.311054 to 0.316818, which does not establish global scaffold collapse. Together these observations support a loss of access to larger improvements through the proposal scheme, rather than a shortage of valid molecules or enough evidence to diagnose surrogate failure. A topology-changing graph proposal operator or a search scheme that preserves access to distinct ring/linker arrangements is the kind of method that could address that limitation; its benefit remains untested. Reactive oxygen/nitrogen decorations and unspecified stereochemistry persist, so removing crossover did not establish chemically reliable generation. The measured contribution belongs to the total adaptive route, including its finishing access and changed random histories. Fragment construction, finishing and chemical mediation remain inseparable here; the sign is not a significance claim and does not transfer automatically to a different score model or end the broader approach.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen Search sessions completed. Across 73,861 breeding attempts, 33,506 retained random draws would have entered the old crossover route, yet there were zero partner draws, crossover constructions or finishing calls. Recombinant purchases fell from 1,480 to zero; all 4,350 Child purchases had one generating parent and complete provenance joins. Every paid stream diverged at its first proposal. Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.978073 to 5.205729 over 4,350 purchases, and late mass fell from 1.022408 to 0.990278 over 2,175 purchases. The complete mean fell from 0.607030 to 0.555541, a paired change of -0.051490; the three seed changes were -0.106268, -0.027952 and -0.020249. Ten task/seed endpoints declined and five improved. Task-average changes were -0.168953 for sitagliptin, -0.091639 for scaffold hopping, -0.011228 for median similarity, +0.002993 for docking and +0.011379 for zaleplon. No registered falsifier triggered. This supports positive conditional contribution of the retained crossover route at the registered 0.002 descriptive scale, despite the Child scoring worse.

molecular.headline: Medium-sized, ring-rich aromatic molecules retain reactive halogen and peroxide motifs and omit stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This is an assessment of n-060debe936b2 and its exact Parent n-cf8d309c06de using only the frozen Search seeds 0/1/2. Child evaluation and Parent pairing are both complete, as separately recorded by context.comparison; all 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectories were read, with no missing path or absent comparison. Each side contains 4,350 accepted optimizer records, plus 150 supplied initial records that are excluded from proposal statistics. No unpurchased proposals, heldout evidence or Confirmation evidence is characterized. The Child produces connected, predominantly aromatic, multiring molecules with carbonyls, ethers, nitrogen heterocycles, amines and frequent halogens. All 4,350 parse with RDKit; parsing does not establish stability or a synthesis. Heavy atoms span 22–47 with median 32, versus Parent 1–96 with median 28. Child counts below 6, below 12 and above 50 heavy atoms are all zero; Parent counts are 91, 124 and 44 respectively. Child ring counts span 1–10, median 4, and aromatic-ring median is 3. The digest independently reports ring-closure rate 1.0 in every task and aromatic-atom presence 0.9966–1.0; those text rates are molecule presence indicators, not aromatic atom fractions. Nonempty typed/generic Bemis–Murcko scaffold counts are 1,762/878 in the Child versus 1,667/951 in the Parent: typed variety is substantial, but generic topology coverage is smaller. Mean within-session Morgan Tanimoto similarity is 0.316818 versus 0.296088; requiring both molecules to have at least 12 heavy atoms gives 0.316818 versus 0.311054. Thus fragment removal changes the comparison materially and a broad collapse claim is unwarranted. Child nitrogen–halogen, oxygen–halogen and peroxide-bearing molecule counts are 882, 487 and 264 versus Parent 888, 162 and 118. These overlapping motif counts describe liability exposure, not measured instability or component attribution. There are 86 Child molecules with an RDKit-perceived all-aromatic ring of size at most four, warranting geometric review, versus 170 in the Parent. There are 2,619 Child molecules with detectable unassigned stereocentres and no specified atom stereochemistry. Conventional cores coexist with strained or reactive decorations; medicinal appearance is moderate and synthetic plausibility is questionable, not uniformly impossible. Auditable definitions, all cell statistics and exact underlying run-relative file citations are in policy/scratch/r0061-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json; byte hashes and trusted original paths are in policy/scratch/r0061-03-improve-L01/molecular/input-manifest.json; quoted-molecule receipts are in policy/scratch/r0061-03-improve-L01/molecular/citation-validation.json. The association of chemistry with scores does not determine operator activation, causal contribution, or biological utility.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 paid molecules stay at 22–28 heavy atoms, median 25. They are compact aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl compounds, often indole-like amides, with alkoxy/alkyl substitution and occasional fused nitrogen bridges. The seed-0 leader is an open enamine bearing two N–F bonds; seed 1 has an indole carboxamide bearing N–Cl and an N-hydroxy substituent; seed 2 has a fused nitrogen-containing aromatic ketone. These are recognizable medicinal-sized cores, but the first two leaders have questionable reactive decorations. The Parent leaders also occupy compact aromatic carbonyl chemistry and include N-halogen liabilities; this is no categorical change from absent to present ring chemistry.
liabilities: Nitrogen–halogen bonds occur in 338 of 870 paid molecules; an N-hydroxy substituent and imine/enamine motifs add reactive or tautomeric ambiguity in cited leaders.
Many candidates are flat aromatic systems. The aromatic ketone leader is chemically more conventional than the halogenated nitrogen leaders, but no synthesis or property assessment was supplied.
missing_features: The higher-score set does not demonstrate consistently stable alternatives across its distinct carbonyl/heteroaryl arrangements: two seed leaders retain nitrogen-bound halogen, whereas the other shows this is not obligatory.
No particular absent pharmacophore can be inferred from these trajectories. Nitriles are absent from the paid set, but the observed scores do not establish that adding one would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited seed-0 low proposal, an expanded partly saturated sulfur-substituted indole carboxamide, scores 0.021623282473063696. The respective seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.44080749154906895, 0.44989726212142783 and 0.4562193134122328, while Parent leaders score 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554. The visible gradient associates compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements and changed heteroatom placement with higher scores, without uniquely rewarding an amide: the seed-2 ketone also scores well. The seeds differ chemically, so the N-halogen motif is neither a universal requirement nor evidence of useful reactivity.

per_task.generated_character: The paid molecules span 22–47 heavy atoms, median 34, and combine extended aromatic/heteroaromatic rings with amino links, imines and carbonyl-containing nitrogen rings. The seed-0 leader is a fused heteroaromatic system joined through a fluorinated amino linkage; seed 1 is a larger assembly with hydrazone and N-chloro motifs; seed 2 carries an allene, peroxide, hypochlorite and N–F bond on a multiring heteroaromatic core. The latter combinations make apparent synthesis and isolation particularly questionable. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 285/164 versus Parent 346/240, so ring abundance coexists with reduced topology coverage.
liabilities: Of 870 proposals, 213 bear peroxides, 167 oxygen–halogen bonds and 206 nitrogen–halogen bonds. These classes overlap and include the best-scoring seed-2 molecule.

Hydrazones, cumulated unsaturation and fused ring edits require stability and geometry scrutiny. Forty-four paid molecules have an RDKit-perceived all-aromatic ring of at most four atoms; perception alone does not establish a realizable geometry.
missing_features: The Child high-score set does not reproduce the Parent seed-0 fused heteroaromatic carbonyl/thione arrangement, despite ample aromatic rings. This is an observed coverage gap, not proof that any single missing group explains the score.

There is no demonstrated route to similarly elaborate, stable linked-ring products without accumulating reactive oxygen and nitrogen decorations; a universal required decoration cannot be recovered from the supplied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited lower proposal, a chromenone-like core with an extended unsaturated nitrile-bearing substituent, scores 0.5153272576636289. The seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.6143330571665286, 0.615474024661411 and 0.6173879243327287. Higher scores associate with densely substituted, nitrogen-rich linked/fused aromatic structures, but the small separation between structurally different leaders does not identify a useful peroxide or hypochlorite contribution. The Parent seed-0 leader scores 0.8561477222467935 with a five-ring, carbonyl/thione heteroaromatic architecture; it also contains an oxygen–fluorine bond and a chlorinated ether. The other Parent leader scores are 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496. The Parent comparison therefore supplies alternative topologies rather than a chemically clean target to copy.

per_task.generated_character: This set spans 25–44 heavy atoms, median 37, with halogenated phenyl groups, phenols/ethers, amine-rich saturated rings, bridges and flexible nitrogen linkers. The seed-0 leader has a phenol, difluoroaryl ring, secondary amine and bridged amino/aminal-like ring system; seed 1 contains an aziridine, imine, amine linker and amide; seed 2 combines an aminal-like ring with an aryl sulfoxide and a fused aromatic ether system. Basic amine capability and mixed aromatic/saturated character are clearly present. Some fragments are conventional, but unusual bridges, small rings and unspecified stereochemistry complicate synthetic plausibility. The Child median exceeds the Parent median of 29 heavy atoms; all Parent seed leaders are also aromatic amine-containing molecules.
liabilities: The cited leaders include aziridine and aminal-like motifs, complex bridges, or sulfoxide stereochemistry; their stability, stereoisomer composition and accessible conformations have not been measured.
Neutral SMILES can represent protonatable amines, so the zero charged-string rate does not mean zero basicity. It also does not establish which protonation state was evaluated.
missing_features: The missing capability is controlled realization of the observed amine/aromatic arrangements: none specifies atom stereochemistry, despite 868 of 870 molecules having a detectable unassigned centre.
No separate absent binding group is established. The high scores already occur with basic amines; chemically simpler, stereodefined equivalents of these leaders remain unshown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited acid/amide/sulfonamide-rich low molecule scores 0.007354407913688945, whereas the seed-0/1/2 amine-rich leaders score 0.9999873649964273, 0.9895517985733925 and 0.9731550514562216. Relative to those lows, the visible high-score chemistry preserves halogenated aromatic surfaces while presenting accessible amine centres and more saturated geometry. Parent leaders score 0.980206046238846, 0.9999921067161532 and 0.9735180254338864, including a more compact halogenated aryl cyclic-aminal structure in seed 1. These scores associate amine placement and scaffold shape with the trajectory gradient; they do not validate binding, protonation state, or stereoisomer-specific activity.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals occupy 29–40 heavy atoms, median 34. Aromatic panels are linked or fused to medium/large nitrogen-containing rings bearing lactam/urea-like carbonyls, N-methyl substituents and exocyclic alkenes. The seed-0 leader has a dibenzofused oxygen-containing ring connected through an alkene to an N-methylated cyclic urea-like ring; seed 1 adds a spiro carbonyl system with N–O/N–N/O–S connectivity; seed 2 has fused nitrogen rings bearing carbonyls and two aryl substituents. There is substantial ring variety: 537 typed and 325 generic scaffolds versus Parent 559 and 379. These are complex heterocyclic series, with a recognizable carbonyl/amine vocabulary but uncertain synthesis for the spiro and heteroatom-rich examples.
liabilities: Medium/large ring closures, spiro links and exocyclic alkenes create conformational and synthetic uncertainty; the seed-1 leader specifically contains unusual N–O/N–N/O–S linkages.

Carbonyl functionality is present in 868 of 870 paid molecules, so an absence-of-carbonyl explanation is contradicted. No molecule specifies atom stereochemistry despite 633 with detectable unassigned centres.
missing_features: The high-score set does not consistently reach compact fused nitrogen/carbonyl topologies without enlarged or unusually heteroatom-linked rings; the paired example shows that larger structures are not necessary for the higher observed score.
Stereodefined versions and a broader set of chemically conventional ways to arrange the existing aromatic/carbonyl features are unshown; the data do not justify prescribing one specific scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited lower polyene/thione-containing molecule scores 0.12755766144221392. Seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.22581950665015363, 0.22016363277743922 and 0.20682086236631844. The visible improvement accompanies retention of aromatic regions while reorganizing carbonyl-bearing nitrogen rings, adding saturated linkers and changing ring fusion; it does not show that size growth alone is rewarded. Parent leader scores are 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313. The last is a 31-heavy-atom fused nitrogen/carbonyl structure, compared with 35 heavy atoms in the corresponding Child leader. The higher Parent example supports considering compact topology coverage, but neither the ceiling nor these structures identifies a unique absent functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The paid molecules have 26–32 heavy atoms, median 29, and combine nitrogen-rich fused aromatic carbonyl/imine cores with fluorinated carbon rings and frequent heteroatom halogenation. The seed-0 leader is a highly bridged/caged nitrogen heterocycle with an aryl hypofluorite; seed 1 has an N-linked difluoroamino group and a fluorinated carbonyl substituent; seed 2 bears a difluorocyclopropyl group, a fluorinated thiol-bearing cyclopentene, a formate ester and N–F. Several motifs are individually recognizable, but their combination and the cage connectivity make isolation and synthesis questionable. Parent leaders include less bridged fluorinated unsaturated rings with related carbonyl/imino heterocycles, although their N–F or small-ring liabilities remain.
liabilities: Nitrogen–halogen bonds occur in 272 of 870 proposals and oxygen–halogen bonds in 222. Peroxide, thiol/geminal-thiol and small-ring variants also appear; these are concrete stability or geometry concerns, not measured failures.

There are no specified atom stereocentres despite 723 molecules with detectable unassigned centres. Neutral aromatic encodings and exocyclic imines also leave tautomer/protonation interpretation unresolved.
missing_features: The Child leaders do not consistently combine the less bridged fluorinated-ring arrangements seen among the higher Parent examples with credible, stable heteroatom chemistry; neither N–F nor an O–F substitution can be called a required feature.
Stereodefined versions of the fluorinated and thiol-bearing saturated centres are absent. The trajectories do not establish whether specifying configuration would change the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited lower expanded nitrogen heterocycle scores 5.789136455227341e-13; seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.4362199094553492, 0.5113200681261488 and 0.5759535156421196. Within this sampled chemistry, higher scores associate with compact fluorinated ring arrangements and retained carbonyl/imino groups. The matched Parent leader scores are 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813. The seed-2 late proposal at evaluation 295 adds an amino-substituted formate-bearing carbon to a closely related fluorinated scaffold and scores only 0.0007017783998135413. That low neighbor cautions against a monotone more-fluorine or more-amine explanation: the trajectory reveals a sharply structure-dependent combined score, not the effect of an isolated functional group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-060debe936b2, complete accepted Search panel 0/1/2, 300 observations per session including ten initial records, batch ten. Among its 4,350 optimizer molecules, 882 have nitrogen–halogen bonds, 487 oxygen–halogen bonds and 264 peroxide bonds; exact Parent n-cf8d309c06de has 888, 162 and 118. Quoted leaders include these motifs. The counts overlap and are structural observations, not stability measurements or attribution to a component. Exact input provenance and definitions are in policy/scratch/r0061-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and input-manifest.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable functional-group construction is inconsistent: reactive heteroatom halogenation and peroxide connectivity persist beside conventional aromatic carbonyl and amine chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs a way to distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogen and stable oxygen/nitrogen groups from reactive heteroatom-bound variants while retaining scaffold and functional-group diversity. Those alternatives must be evaluated using current-session observations; the counts do not establish that blanket rejection will improve any score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-060debe936b2 under the same complete Search panel and profile: zero of 4,350 optimizer molecules specifies atom stereochemistry, while RDKit detects unassigned centres in 2,619. Digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in every task. The exact Parent also has zero specified atom stereochemistry and 2,578 molecules with unassigned centres. The cited amine bridges, fluorinated saturated rings and spiro systems exhibit the relevant ambiguity; no measured stereoisomer score comparison exists.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not resolve stereochemistry even when repeated ring edits create stereogenic saturated structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general molecular representation would need to preserve or deliberately assign feasible stereochemical alternatives when stereogenic centres are created, and record the representation actually passed for evaluation. Protonatable neutral structures also require consistent state handling, but neutral text alone is not evidence of missing basicity. No task identity, external labels or presumed stereoisomer reward is warranted.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-060debe936b2, accepted Search seeds 0/1/2 only: 1,762 typed but 878 generic nonempty scaffolds versus exact Parent 1,667 and 951; 86 Child molecules contain an RDKit-perceived all-aromatic ring of at most four atoms versus 170 Parent molecules. Quoted leaders additionally contain bridged cages, aziridines and expanded heterocycles. Child heavy atoms are restricted to 22–47; Parent spans 1–96, including both fragments and an oversized tail. After excluding molecules below 12 heavy atoms, within-session similarity is 0.316818 versus 0.311054, so these observations do not establish global structural collapse. They are conditional chemistry associations from this panel.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring connectivity is diverse, but dependable access to geometrically credible and compact alternatives is incomplete.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to expand feasible ring/linker arrangements while checking small fused-ring and bridge geometry and retaining compact candidates. Raw typed-scaffold count and removal of both molecular-size tails should not substitute for chemically meaningful coverage. The evidence does not prescribe a particular scaffold, operator, or future experiment.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
